title: Option set
description: One known list of values, shared by every field that points at it (field.optionSet, or a semantic type's display.optionSet), so every endpoint draws the same value with the same label, tone and order. Data display contract, layer 1; the sets themselves are data in devops.option_sets (migration 435), published as schema/option-sets.json. A status option takes its state's tone; a value with no tone falls back to the default tone map in display-rules.json (toneMap).

key.description: The set's key: a shared set is one word (workflow_status, iso_country); a set owned by one field is <owner>.<field> (relay.status, goal.priority). Sets derived from a semantic type's own options are semantic.<type>.

label.description: What the set is, for people: 'Relay status'.

kind.description: status: values are states, each with a state and its tone (dot in a cell, chip elsewhere). choice: categories, each toned (chip, segmented or select by count). code: a generated list of codes from a standard (generator), untoned, picked with search.

ordinal.description: The order means something (low < urgent), so sorting follows the list, not the alphabet. An ordinal choice set draws its tones as a ramp in that order (display-rules.json ramp).

generator.description: For a code set: the standard its full list comes from (iso_3166_1_alpha2, iso_4217, iana_tz …). Until it is generated the set holds samples.

description.description: One line on what the set is for.

label.description: What is shown. Defaults to the value.

state.description: For a status set: which of the five groups the option is in. Its tone is the state's: done lime, moving sky, waiting amber, failed rose, ended neutral.

description.description: One line shown in pickers and tooltips.

live.description: The state is in motion (running, syncing): the dot pulses.
